checks.output: 32 runbook rows, each naming trigger, owner and reversibility, all with documentation_only true and steps empty. Measured honestly: 0 of 32 procedures are written (the corpus names the runbooks and contains none of their steps), owner is null with reason unassigned-in-corpus on 32 of 32 because no checked-in document assigns one, and reversibility is stated by policy for 2 rows (read-only-no-mutation for diagnostic capture, reversible-by-inverse-transition for a safety-mode transition) and unassigned-in-corpus for 30. 19 rows are production-touching and none can carry a step. notes: Honest state of the inventory. (1) Owner assignment is the dominant gap, not an oversight: 70 of 130 entries record owner null with reason unassigned-in-corpus, including 13 of 14 retention classes, 7 of 10 credential classes and 32 of 32 runbooks. Policy in operations-and-governance.md requires an owner for each of those and the checked-in corpus assigns none, so the measurement is that the assignment work does not exist yet; inventing owners would have been the failure mode. (2) No deployed instance is recorded anywhere — no tenant, actor, credential, workspace or budget value — because this is a clean-room repository and the running system is not reachable from it; those are the 24 enumerated gaps, 9 of them not-reachable-from-repository. (3) The judgement the contract flags is implemented as: record class, owner and shape; withhold the value as two enums (shape plus reason) with no free-text field, so 'record the shape' cannot become a place to write the value. (4) The checker is deliberately NOT wired into plan/check.py: several items were in flight and that file is a collision point. tools/surface_inventory/verify.py is standalone with its own main() returning an exit status; wiring it into plan/check.py or the plan workflow is the follow-up for the integrator, and until then the inventory is checked only when that command is run. (5) The number-versus-citation rule was strengthened mid-item after a command-line break showed the first version accepted a recalled 90-day TTL parked beside an unrelated citation; it now requires the quoted words to contain the number beside its unit. (6) Self-review found and removed four classes of over-claim before finishing, where a field asserted a per-class value the corpus never assigns: credential storage class (9 of 10 now unspecified-in-corpus, since policy names three preferred mechanisms and selects none per class; only the escrowed-ciphertext class is stated), artifact visibility (12 of 12 now unassigned-in-corpus, with a gap recording that policy requires distinct visibility classes and assigns none), budget enforcement point (all nine scheduler budgets are now 'both', which is what the policy actually says, instead of a per-bullet split that was invented), and workspace release promotability (only the dirty-source capture is stated not-promotable). The repository-owner role's authority was narrowed to select-work after re-reading GOVERNANCE.md: the owner configures integration policy, the bounded integrator integrates. (7) Reported as input to R1-13 and R0-10; neither is claimed satisfied. R0-10 consumes plan/inventory/surface/restore-dependencies.json, which carries the ordered dependency list and the two declared objectives but no measured restore timing — that measurement is R0-10's to make.
